name: Strawberry
notes: Aroma is fragile — strongly favour secondary additions.

name: Raspberry
notes: Intensely flavoured; 0.2 kg/L is already assertive. Seeds add mild tannin.

name: Blackberry
notes: Pairs with buckwheat and baking spice; seeds add tannin.

name: Blueberry
notes: Subtle in mead; use heavy loads (0.35+ kg/L) and crush or freeze first.

name: Cherry (sweet)
notes: Needs added acid for balance. Mass is pitted weight.

name: Cherry (tart / Montmorency)
notes: Classic cyser/melomel fruit; self-balancing acidity. Mass is pitted weight.

name: Peach
notes: Volatile aroma; use pectic enzyme. Mass is pitted weight.

name: Apricot
notes: Pectin-heavy — pectic enzyme is mandatory for clarity.

name: Plum
notes: Skins carry colour and tannin. Mass is pitted weight.

name: Apple (as whole fruit)
notes: For cyser, using pressed juice (insoluble = 0) is far more practical.

name: Apple juice (cyser)
notes: Enter juice as mass (≈ 1.046 kg/L). Preservative-free only (no sorbate/benzoate).

name: Pear
notes: Low acid and delicate; pair with light honey; acid adjustment likely.

name: Grape (wine, pyment)
notes: Pyment. Grapes bring significant YAN and fermentable sugar.

name: Mango
notes: Low acid, thick pulp. Mass is peeled, pitted weight.

name: Pineapple
notes: Bromelain; tropical, pairs with ginger and coconut.

name: Black currant
notes: Extremely acidic and tannic; 0.1–0.2 kg/L is usually enough.

name: Elderberry (cooked/dried only)
notes: Raw elderberries are toxic — use cooked or dried, ripe fruit only. Very tannic.

name: Cranberry
notes: Very low pH — high pH-crash risk in primary.

name: Pomegranate (arils)
notes: Tannic; best as juice.

name: Banana
notes: Mostly used for body; very low acid; peeled weight.
